question: What two bodily functions permanently stop during clinical death?
explanation: Clinical death is officially marked by the irreversible cessation of both blood circulation and breathing. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why must a nurse quickly identify the signs of clinical death?

options.A: To immediately discharge the room for a new admission
options.B: To prevent the family from seeing the deceased patient
options.C: To bypass the need for a physician's physical examination
options.D: To avoid unnecessary resuscitation and maintain dignity

explanation: Recognizing irreversible death stops futile chest compressions and preserves the peace and dignity of the person. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which pupillary finding is expected during an assessment for irreversible death?
explanation: Brainstem death causes pupils to remain wide open and fail to react to light. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h2)

question: A patient shows no breathing or carotid pulse. What immediate assessment confirms lack of brainstem reflex?

options.A: Testing deep tendon reflexes in the knee
options.B: Measuring blood pressure with a manual cuff
options.D: Auscultating bowel sounds in four quadrants

explanation: Testing pupil reaction to light helps verify brainstem death alongside breathing and pulse checks. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h2)

question: For how long should a nurse listen with a stethoscope to confirm absent heart sounds?
explanation: Listening for a full minute ensures that faint, slow, or irregular heartbeats are not missed. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h3)

question: Which artery is most appropriate to check for central pulses during a death assessment?
explanation: Central major arteries like the carotid provide the most reliable indication of remaining systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h3)

question: Who has the ultimate legal authority to officially pronounce and certify death in a hospital setting?
explanation: Only a qualified doctor can legally sign a death certificate and pronounce a patient dead. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse when a patient passes away unexpectedly?

options.A: Complete and sign the official government death certificate
options.B: Immediately move the body to the external morgue
options.C: Inform the police without notifying the medical team
options.D: Assess vital signs and report findings to the doctor

explanation: Nurses gather clinical evidence and notify the physician so official certification can take place. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h4)

question: What type of language should a nurse use when writing post-mortem nursing notes?
explanation: Medical records require strictly factual information without subjective emotional language. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h5)

question: Which detail is most critical to include in the death documentation?

options.A: Personal opinion on the cause of the underlying illness
options.B: Exact time vital signs ceased and physician was notified
options.C: Names of all visitors who arrived during visiting hours
options.D: Detailed financial status of the surviving family members

explanation: A precise timeline protects the hospital and staff by clearly showing when clinical events and notifications occurred. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h5)

question: Why should limbs be aligned in a natural position shortly after death?

options.A: To prevent the development of hospital-acquired infections
options.B: To speed up the natural cooling process of the body
options.C: To make it easier for relatives to perform an autopsy
options.D: To prevent difficult positioning caused by rigor mortis

explanation: Stiffening of muscles begins soon after death, making proper alignment difficult if delayed. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h6)

question: What personal protective equipment is necessary when performing post-mortem care?

options.A: Full hazmat suit with a powered air-purifying respirator
options.B: Sterile surgical gown and double face shields only
options.C: No special equipment is needed once the patient has expired
options.D: Standard gloves and apron due to potential fluid exposure

explanation: Universal precautions apply because post-mortem leakage of blood and body fluids remains a biological hazard. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is the best way to communicate news of a patient's death to family members?

options.A: Use vague euphemisms to soften the emotional blow
options.B: Use clear, direct language in a private room
options.C: Send a text message before they arrive at the hospital
options.D: Speak loudly across the crowded nursing station

explanation: Clear and direct wording prevents misunderstandings, and a private room maintains dignity and privacy. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h7)

question: A grieving family requests specific religious rites for their deceased relative before transfer. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Accommodate the request safely according to hospital guidelines
options.B: Ask another family member to overrule their religious wishes
options.C: Insist that the body be moved to the basement right away
options.D: Refuse immediately because mortuary protocols cannot change

explanation: Respecting cultural and religious traditions is a core component of holistic, compassionate end-of-life care. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h7)
